newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VICENZA STAY TOP BUT COACH WORRIED ABOUT RELEGATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICENZA STAY TOP BUT COACH WORRIED ABOUT RELEGATION.

text.p: Vicenza coach Franceso Guidolin watched his side draw 1-1 at Perugia on Sunday to restore their historic one-point lead over Internazionale at the top of serie A -- and then warned about the threat of relegation.
"Our aim at the start of the season was to avoid relegation from the first division," said Guidolin, whose team is setting the pace in serie A for the first time in their 94-year history.
"Only when that aim is achieved can we start thinking about other objectives like the championship."
Alessandro Iannuzzi, a close season buy from Lazio, moved Vicenza closer to first division salvation when a 10th minute shot from the edge of the penalty area put his side 1-0 up.

Carmine Gautieri equalised for Perugia in the 33rd, but the away point was enough to give unfancied Vicenza 21 points from 11 matches, one more than Inter, who had briefly drawn level on Saturday after drawing 2-2 at home to Cagliari.

With the league's top two clubs due to meet next week, Intercontinental Cup winners Juventus moved ominously into third after defeating Bologna courtesy of Zinedine Zidane's superbly struck 50th minute free kick.
The Turin side are level on 19 points with Bologna, two behind Vicenza, but have played a game less than their rivals.
Before their match with Bologna, Juventus paraded the European and Intercontinental Cups at the Stadio delle Alpi.

Marcello Lippi's side then set about demonstrating how they intend adding this season's league title to their trophy room, shrugging off jet lag from their midweek triumph over River Plate in Tokyo to outclass the visitors.
Alessandro Del Piero, Juve's match-winner against River Plate, nearly repeated the feat in the 23rd minute, slipping his marker but finding the far post with a diagonal shot.
In the second half, Del Piero ran over the ball at a free kick to leave Frenchman Zidane to calmly stroke the ball over Bologna's defensive wall and into the net.
Napoli dropped to fifth place, two points behind Juventus, after drawing 2-2 at Atalanta.

Despite having their Argentine captain Roberto Ayala sent off in the fourth minute for violent conduct and seeing Nicola Caccia miss the target with a first half spot kick, Napoli led 2-1 with 15 minutes to play.
But, bouncing back from Andrea Sottil's dismissal, the Bergamo side salvaged a point with Marco Sgro's late goal.

Stung by rumours of George Weah's departure for Arsenal and shocked by their Italian Cup quarter-final elimination to Vicenza last week, AC Milan's already black season turned even darker with a 3-2 defeat at Piacenza.
Playing in front of a defence without suspended Paolo Maldini and injured Christian Panucci, goalkeeper Sebastiano Rossi had a nightmare first half.
First, he fumbled a speculative 25-metre effort from Aladino Valoti; then, a Franco Baresi back pass was cleared straight to Eusebio De Francesco, who made it 2-0.

Coach Oscar Washington Tabarez brought on Dejan Savicevic and Christophe Dugarry and the Frenchman pulled a goal back with his first touch -- chesting a cross down and shooting home in one smooth movement for his first-ever Milan goal.
In the 68th minute, Dugarry levelled the scores but as Milan started to think about three points, Pasquale Luiso struck with a breathtaking winner -- his eighth goal of the season.

Milan's fourth defeat of the season was a severe blow ahead of Wednesday's European Cup Champions' League match with Rosenborg -- a game they must not lose if they want to stay in this season's competition.
Like Milan, Parma are also struggling to come to terms with a new manager, Carlo Ancelotti, slipping to their fourth defeat of the season, 3-1 at Udinese.
New coach Francesco Oddo failed to lift Reggiana's spirits or bottom-of-the-table position, watching his side fall to late Lazio goals from Pavel Nedved and Italy's Pierluigi Casiraghi.
